NASA MGS MOLA Global DEM · via NASA JPL Mars Trek elevation-profile service · Regional (~463 m MOLA detail). Not for walking-scale terrain. MOLA only across the whole area: the sharper HRSC-derived detail seen in parts of the hillshade is not in this layer. Tiles end at zoom 9; closer zooms enlarge them. Values are MGS MOLA heights as returned by the Mars Trek elevation-profile service, interpolated by that service onto a 0.01 degree grid (about 0.59 km); the service does not state its interpolation method. Plain colour by height class (100 m steps, open-ended outer classes covering -3791 to -2381 m); no shading. Not a slope or safety assessment.

Coverage: MOLA elevations over the team-chosen Oxia display area, 17.11-19.15 N, 334.60-336.60 E, from the 201 x 205 elevation grid (/maps/oxia/elevation-grid.json): range -3791 to -2381 m. 26 display tiles, zooms 5-9, built by team/oxia/terrain/build_elevation_tiles.mjs.

NASA MGS MOLA and ESA Mars Express HRSC hillshade blend · via NASA JPL Mars Trek · Regional relief only, 200 m per pixel. Not for walking-scale slope or safety. Detail varies: sharp where Mars Express HRSC stereo elevation exists (e.g. the south-east of the area), smoother where only MOLA (~463 m) is available (much of the centre). A per-tile edge check at zoom 9 found smooth tiles across roughly 17.98-19.15 N, 334.60-336.09 E (including the area around the Clay-rich bedrock study target) and crisp tiles south of about 18 N and east of about 336.1 E; Mars Trek does not state which input each pixel comes from, so this is an inference from the image. Tiles end at zoom 9; closer zooms enlarge them. Shaded relief image with no elevation or slope values; boulders, small craters and steep local slopes are not resolved. Illumination direction is not stated by Mars Trek. Display-grade, nearest-neighbour resampled from Mars Trek JPEG tiles (lossy compression). No routing or hazard use.

Coverage: Mars Trek MOLA + HRSC hillshade blend over the team-chosen Oxia display area, 17.11-19.15 N, 334.60-336.60 E: 26 derived display tiles, Web-Mercator XYZ, zooms 5-9 (source level 8, about 163 m per pixel; product 200 m per pixel). No gaps in this area.

>20 degrees: regional numerical slope class. MOLA (~463 m) does not resolve small steep features. Not an astronaut safety threshold.

NASA MGS MOLA Global DEM · via NASA JPL Mars Trek elevation-profile service · Regional slope from MOLA (~463 m). Small banks, boulders and walking-scale hazards are not resolved. Not a safety assessment. MOLA only across the whole area: the sharper HRSC-derived detail seen in parts of the hillshade is not in this layer. Tiles end at zoom 9; closer zooms enlarge them. Slope from central differences on a 0.01 degree grid interpolated from MOLA, using Mars 2000 sphere distances (R = 3,396,190 m); steep short slopes are smoothed out, so real local slopes can exceed the mapped class. The >20 degree class marks slopes beyond NASA's 20 degree suited-walking figure: NASA EVA-EXP-0042 Rev B, Exploration EVA System Concept of Operations (Oct 19, 2020), p.38, 'Walking up/down/across a slope of up to 20°' (source oxia-nasa-eva-exp-0042); NASA ICES-2025-129 (Kim et al., funded by the NASA Mars Campaign Office), p.7, treats slopes beyond +/-20 degrees as inaccessible no-go zones (source oxia-nasa-ices-2025-129). That figure is lunar-derived and Mars gravity is higher. In this area 56 of 41,205 cells (18.8 km2, 0.14%) exceed 20 degrees, mostly one patch near 17.21 N, 335.07 E.

Coverage: Slope in degrees over the team-chosen Oxia display area, 17.11-19.15 N, 334.60-336.60 E, from a 201 x 205 elevation grid (0.01 degree, about 0.59 km) sampled from the Mars Trek elevation-profile service (MGS MOLA, Global DEM). 26 display tiles, zooms 5-9. Grid: /maps/oxia/elevation-grid.json.

Red-pink: middle

Dark purple: darkest, cools fast at night (likely loose sand or dust)

NASA Mars Odyssey THEMIS · night-IR global mosaic (2018 release) · via NASA JPL Mars Trek · Relative brightness only: the 8-bit mosaic values are not calibrated temperatures and are not thermal-inertia values. Observation period not stated by Mars Trek (the 'oct2018' in the layer name refers to the 2018 mosaic release). Night-time brightness mainly reflects thermal inertia (brighter = holds heat, e.g. rock or indurated surfaces; darker = loose sand or dust), but it can also vary with season, local time and dust. Mosaic of many orbits with stretched brightness between images, so strip-to-strip seams can appear. Colours are a display ramp (matplotlib 'inferno') applied to the uncalibrated 8-bit values; they do not mark temperature or thermal-inertia thresholds. Display-grade, nearest-neighbour resampled; not terrain-safety evidence.

Coverage: Mars Trek THEMIS night-IR global mosaic over the team-chosen Oxia display area, 17.11-19.15 N, 334.60-336.60 E: 75 derived display tiles, Web-Mercator XYZ, zooms 5-10 (source level 9, about 81 m per pixel), coloured with an inferno display ramp. No gaps in this area.
